patch.value:
## Problem
Correct authorship currently depends on every agent remembering to prefix mutations with PM_AUTHOR. That is out-of-band instruction cost on every call, it is silently skippable, and when skipped it produces unknown-author history events that the governance surface then has to triage.

## Approach
Resolve identity from the runtime instead of from instruction. A harness detector inspects environment markers and process ancestry to name the acting agent, and the result is recorded alongside a provenance discriminator so that detected identity is never mistaken for cryptographically verified identity.

## Boundary
Detection is convenience, not authentication. Verifiable authorship is pm-u14c (per-entry signatures); authorization is pm-xc68 (principal policy). This item must not claim or imply verification, and strict-mode rejection semantics stay owned by the attribution enforcement work.

## Prior art in this workspace
Ergonomic attribution (global --author, init author_default, unknown-author advisory) and attribution enforcement both shipped and closed; the telemetry agent-identity dimension already hashes PM_AUTHOR. This item adds the detection layer those three assumed would exist.
Harness-aware author identity: pm resolves the acting agent from its runtime harness so PM_AUTHOR is never required

A public SDK resolver detects the acting harness from environment and process ancestry, covering at minimum Claude Code, Codex, pi, opencode, Cursor, Aider, Gemini CLI, and generic CI, with an extension point for unknown harnesses; Resolution precedence is documented and tested: explicit --author, then PM_AUTHOR, then configured author_default, then harness detection, then anonymous; Every history entry records an author_source discriminator (asserted vs detected vs configured) so detected identity is never confused with verified identity; Detection is bounded and never blocks: a hard timeout and a pure-function fallback keep cold-start latency within the startup budget; Detected authors are recorded in a stable, greppable namespace (for example harness:claude-code) so downstream queries can filter by harness; Telemetry continues to receive only the hashed author context, with no raw harness-derived identity leaving the machine
An agent runs pm mutations with no identity ceremony and the recorded author is still accurate and provenanced

Every mutation an agent makes today must be prefixed with an environment variable that the agent has to be told about out of band; that prefix is pure token and instruction overhead repeated on every call.
Removes the single most repeated piece of boilerplate in agent-facing pm usage and makes author attribution correct by default instead of correct by discipline.

pm create/update/close invoked with no author configuration record a harness-derived author plus an author_source provenance field, and unknown-author events stop being produced by first-party agent runs.
Author attribution enforcement shipped with a strict mode, but strict mode is unusable while correct attribution depends on every agent remembering an env var. Detection is the missing half.

value.note: Existing author-parity coverage this feature extends with harness-resolved identity and author_source provenance
